historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management medium-term organic target (3-4% CAGR), cross-checked against the recast continuing-operations revenue CAGR FY2023 -> FY2026E of 2.75% and 2026 organic growth of 2% / 4% / 5% in Q1 / Q2 / Q3
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity, EPS and FCF CAGRs are not computable on a like-for-like basis: shareholders' equity fell from $23.8B (FY2024) to $14.1B (FY2025) on the Qnity distribution, reported EPS mixes pre- and post-split share counts and discontinued-operations losses, and continuing-operations cash flow before 2026 carries pre-separation interest and stranded costs (CFO less capex: FY2023 $543M, FY2024 $480M, FY2025 $227M, 9M-2026 $793M). The house default of equity CAGR as the growth anchor does not apply; growth is anchored to the recast revenue series and guidance instead.
historical_growth.notes: Only three recast annual revenue points exist for today's two-segment company (FY2023 6,614; FY2024 6,719; FY2025 6,849) plus FY2026E 7,175. SBC is ~1% of revenue, so owner FCF and reported FCF grow at essentially the same rate.

scenario_narratives.base: The two-segment company delivers what it has guided to. Healthcare & Water (47% of sales) grows mid-single digits on Tyvek medical packaging, medical-device contract manufacturing and reverse-osmosis / ion-exchange demand; Diversified Industrials (53%) grows low-single digits with Building Technologies flat-to-up and aerospace and industrial lines recovering. Organic growth runs at the middle of the 3-4% target and fades to 2.5%. Operating EBITDA margin moves from ~24.75% to ~26% as the 2026 restructuring programme and productivity come through, with nothing further assumed. PFAS obligations follow the fixed NJ and NC payment schedules and the remaining AFFF personal-injury docket resolves within the MOU cap at roughly the provision carried in the bridge.
scenario_narratives.bull: Water and healthcare compound faster than the target - desalination, industrial water reuse and semiconductor ultrapure-water projects delayed by the Middle East conflict land in 2027-28, and bolt-ons (Spectrum, Donatelle, Sinochem RO) add capacity into a strong medical-device cycle - while aerospace build rates and a US construction recovery lift Diversified Industrials to 4-5%. Mix shifts toward the higher-margin segment and Operating EBITDA margin reaches ~28%, the level of focused water and life-science materials peers. The market grants a simpler, PFAS-de-risked company a higher terminal multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: Diversified Industrials behaves like the cyclical it is: a construction and industrial downturn in 2027-28 takes revenue down ~3% with decremental margins that give back the 2026 gains, China (10% of sales) weakens on trade action or a revived Tyvek antitrust probe, and stranded costs from the fifth separation since 2021 prove stickier than planned. Growth recovers only to 2-2.5% and Operating EBITDA margin settles near 23.7%, below today's. The PFAS overhang persists - the 11,000+ AFFF personal-injury cases and the Corian Quartz silicosis docket keep the multiple at a discount (13x cap).

valuation_philosophy.summary: DuPont is valued as a mature, moderately cyclical specialty-materials company on unlevered owner FCF built from Operating EBITDA, with the non-operating pieces left by five years of separations - the Arclin and Derby stakes, the Aramids note, pension underfunding, noncontrolling interests and the PFAS/MOU obligations - handled once each in the equity bridge. All per-share figures are on the post-reverse-split count of ~133M shares. SBC is ~1% of revenue, so the house/street band is narrow and the valuation turns on the margin path and the terminal multiple, not on compensation accounting.
key_risks_to_valuation: Only three quarters of clean history exist for the current portfolio; the FY2026E base rests on guidance and on a 2026 margin step-up (22.3% Q1-2025 to 25.1% Q3-2026) that has not been through a downturn
PFAS: the $300M unaccrued-tail provision is a judgment; management says it cannot estimate a range above the $459M accrued, and Corian Quartz claims fall outside the MOU cap
Qnity counterparty risk: 44% of MOU funding is recoverable only through Qnity's indemnity
A failed tax-free qualification of the Qnity distribution would create a large uncapped tax liability not modelled here
Terminal value is roughly half of enterprise value and Gordon growth binds close to the 16x cap; a 1pp WACC change moves the base value by roughly 15%
D&A is glided from 8.5% to 5.5% of revenue as acquired intangibles amortise; if the cash tax shield lasts longer, value is modestly understated

inputs.share_count_basis: POST 1-for-3 reverse split (effective 2026-06-24). 132.53M shares outstanding on the Q3-2026 10-Q cover (2026-10-30) plus ~0.8M dilutive options/RSUs/PSUs (Q3 diluted 135.1M less basic 134.3M weighted averages). Held flat because SBC is expensed in the flows. The Metrics.csv FY2025 (419.2M) and Q1-2026 (412.8M) counts are PRE-split and must not be used. The announced $250M Q4-2026 buyback is not yet executed and is not anticipated in the count.
inputs.sbc_source: Q3-2026 10-Q cash flow statement: stock-based compensation $42M for 9M-2026, annualised to $56M; plus employee taxes paid for share-based payment arrangements $24M 9M-2026 (FY2025: $26M; front-loaded in Q1, so ~$27M/yr). DuPont publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed. NOTE: DuPont's Operating EBITDA is struck AFTER stock compensation expense, so the engine's ebitda_margin_path is entered PRE-SBC (Operating EBITDA margin + ~0.8pp) and the sbc_pct_path then charges SBC plus equity-award taxes once.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10-yr UST), ERP ~4.6%, beta ~1.15 -> cost of equity ~9.6%; after-tax cost of debt ~4.1% (BBB+/Baa1); debt ~13% of capital -> WACC ~8.9%, rounded to 9.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclical and PFAS risk is charged in the flows, the scenario weights and the bridge, not again in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases (~$217M liability at FY2025) are already expensed inside Operating EBITDA; lease liabilities are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt (treatment B). No separate lease_cost path.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%); noncontrolling interests deducted once in the equity bridge at ~14x annualised NCI income (~$13M/yr), above the $117M book value.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (US diversified industrial / specialty materials operating company; adaptations file read for the cyclical, NCI, non-operating-asset and risk-charged-once rules). FRESH BUILD - no prior valuation. FY0 is FY2026E at the midpoint of management's net sales guidance ($7,160-7,190M, raised at Q3-2026); 9M-2026 actual is $5,368M. The portfolio only became comparable in 2026: Qnity (Electronics) was spun 2025-11-01 and Aramids sold 2026-04-01, so pre-2025 history is not a trend base; the recast continuing-operations series is FY2023 $6,614M, FY2024 $6,719M, FY2025 $6,849M. reported_fcf is 9M-2026 continuing-operations CFO $1,042M less capex $249M = $793M, annualised (x4/3) to $1,057M; the FY2025 annual figure (CFO $560M - capex $333M = $227M) is NOT a usable base because it carries ~$250M of nine-month interest on ~$4B of since-repaid pre-separation debt, separation costs and indirect costs since removed - it was blank in the CSV and has been read from the FY2025 10-K cash flow statement (line 4666), not defaulted to zero. interest_income is 0 because DuPont is a net-debt company (the engine builds unlevered flows from EBITDA, so interest never enters). Balance sheet is 30 Sep 2026 while flows start FY2027: Q4-2026 cash generation (~$250M FCF before the $0.60 dividend and the planned $250M buyback) is not credited - a small conservative omission. Buybacks: $611M paid 9M-2026 under the $2B authorisation, so the flat share count is funded. FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance $7.47-7.52 is on the post-split ~135M count (~$1.0B adjusted net income), consistent with this model's FY2027 NOPAT of ~$0.9B before interest. Operating EBITDA excludes restructuring, separation and Corian Quartz legal costs; the base margin path carries a 0.5pp/0.3pp haircut in years 1-2 for the 2026 Restructuring Program cash ($100-150M through 2028).

base.margin_note: Entered PRE-SBC: FY2026E Operating EBITDA margin ~24.75% (9M-2026 $1,331M on $5,368M = 24.8%; Q3 25.1%) + ~0.8pp SBC add-back = ~25.5%. Years 1-2 carry a 0.5pp / 0.3pp restructuring-cash haircut. The mature 26.8% equals an Operating EBITDA margin of ~26%, about 0.5-1pp above the 25-25.5% medium-term target management has already reached.
base.da_note: D&A is ~8.6% of revenue today ($620M/yr) because ~$270M/yr is acquisition-intangible amortisation. The path glides to 5.5% as those intangibles run off so the terminal year does not perpetuate an amortisation tax shield over a 4.8% capex rate.
base.wc_note: Negative: receivables + inventory - payables is ~$1.96B, ~27% of revenue, so growth consumes cash.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): more than half of sales are cyclical construction/industrial exposure and the company has only three quarters of history in its current shape, but the balance sheet is investment grade with ~0.8x net debt/EBITDA and no refinancing pressure, and the expected PFAS tail is already charged in the bridge rather than left to the bear case. Base 50%: guidance has been raised through 2026 and the margin target is already met. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): it needs faster water/healthcare growth, a cyclical recovery and a further ~2pp of margin all at once.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
